- Model consistently underestimates prices in early cycles (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon) — adjust downward bias for short-term outlooks.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10–20% above true value) — cap forecast peaks at 1.2x prior high or 1.1x moving average.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to recent volatility — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3–5 day moving average.
- Lagged response: model lags true price movements by 3–7 days — shift forecast horizon forward by 1–2 days for next period.
- High volatility in late forecast period (last 5–10 days) — reduce forecast variance by applying exponential decay weighting (e.g., 0.8 decay factor).
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — don’t extrapolate from last 5 days if history shows no clear trend — use 10–15 day rolling average as anchor.
